content.rendered:
Do not quench the Spirit. Three short words with weight. The Spirit is a fire inside you. The question is whether your daily choices fan the flame or put it out.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, June 10, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Do not quench the Spirit.”
1 Thessalonians 5:19 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes 1 Thessalonians as one of the earliest letters in the entire New Testament. He has just finished a long list of practical instructions for the new church. Rejoice always. Pray continually. Give thanks in every circumstance. And then, in three short Greek words, he says: pneuma me sbennute. Do not quench the Spirit. The verb sbennute is the same verb used for putting out a fire or extinguishing a torch. Paul’s picture is unmistakable. The Spirit in you is a flame, and there is something you can do to put it out.

That is a sobering thought worth sitting with. The Holy Spirit is not so domesticated that He cannot be quieted, ignored, hushed or pushed aside. He is a person. Persons can be grieved. Persons can be quenched. A believer can grow so accustomed to ignoring the Spirit’s nudges, so practised at putting off the conviction He brings, so consistent at saying not now to His promptings, that the inner fire dies down to embers.

How is the Spirit quenched? Scripture gives the inventory. Sustained sin that we refuse to bring to the light. Unforgiveness we will not let go. Bitterness we keep watered. Gossip and corrupting talk. Worldliness we will not name. The shutting down of His voice when He nudges us to do something we do not want to do. Pride that crowds out humility. Busyness that crowds out prayer. Distraction that crowds out worship. None of these are dramatic. All of them, repeated daily, put out the fire.

But the good news is that the same Paul who said do not quench the Spirit also told Timothy to fan into flame the gift of God in him. Quenching is not the only verb available. Fanning is also available. Reading His word fans the flame. Worship fans the flame. Confessing sin fans the flame. Obedience fans the flame. Community with other believers fans the flame. Time alone with God fans the flame. The Spirit responds to attention. The fire grows where it is welcomed.

Today, ask one question. What in my life today might be putting out the fire? Address it. Then ask another. What can I do today that fans the flame? Do it. The Spirit will burn brightly in a life that keeps making space for Him to do so.

Prayer

Holy Spirit, forgive me for every way I have quieted Your voice, ignored Your nudges, or put out Your fire in my life. Today I make space for You. I fan the flame. I welcome Your conviction. I obey Your prompts. Burn brightly in me. Let nothing in my life put You out. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I do not quench the Spirit. I welcome Him. I obey Him. I fan into flame the gift of God in me. The Holy Spirit burns brightly in my life because I keep making space for Him to do so.
